title: ‘No conclusive evidence’ of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane found in the South Pacific
summary: An expedition to find evidence of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane near a remote island in the South Pacific has come up empty, researchers said Sunday. Researchers from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University embarked this month on the Taraia Object expedition in Nikumaroro, an unin...
content:
An expedition to find evidence of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane near a remote island in the South Pacific has come up empty, researchers said Sunday.
Researchers from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University embarked this month on the Taraia Object expedition in Nikumaroro, an uninhabited coral atoll in the Phoenix Islands belonging to the Republic of Kiribati.
The team sought to identify an anomaly first seen in satellite images in 2020. Experts have long suspected Nikumaroro as the landing site of Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, who disappeared in July 1937.
However, the expedition “found no conclusive evidence to confirm a hypothesis that wreckage” from Earhart’s plane was “in a lagoon on a remote atoll in the South Pacific,” the university said in a news release.
“We think it’s most likely that the object was a collection of debris that accumulated here,” Rick Pettigrew, ALI’s executive director, said in a video message.
The expedition determined that the anomaly was most “likely a collection of large trees deposited along the peninsula’s sandpit.” When the team arrived, much of the “debris had fragmented and washed away.” What was left was a Y-shaped segment that was just a small fraction of the anomaly’s original size observed via satellite.

FOR SUBSCRIBERS‘Astounded’: DOJ vets shocked by timing of Ilhan Omar search
The anomaly’s reflective surface, which was “long associated with the idea that the object was a metallic substance,” was found to be a carbonate veneer, meaning it had a layer of carbon-rich sediment.
“We accomplished our goal to determine what the Taraia Object was,” Pettigrew said. “Our team remains in great spirits and proud of what was accomplished.”
Earhart was seeking to be the first woman to fly around the world when she and Noonan disappeared in their Lockheed Electra 10-E.
A U.S. Coast Guard ship lost contact with the pair the morning of July 2, 1937, as they tried to fly to Howland Island, about 400 miles northwest of Nikumaroro.
The expedition to find Earhart’s plane launched from Tarawa in the Republic of Kiribati on Oct. 6 and traveled for five days by sea to Nikumaroro.
While it didn’t crack one of the world’s greatest mysteries, the expedition said the effort strongly supports the broader castaway hypothesis — a theory that Earhart and Noonan didn’t crash into the sea but landed on the flat reef of Nikumaroro and were marooned.
Some artifacts found on the island indicate Earhart and Noonan’s plane may have landed there, including glass bottles from the 1930s and a woman’s makeup compact, the expedition said.
It said it did find “numerous artifacts through both maritime and terrestrial archaeology efforts, including a steel tube about 30 inches long discovered in the lagoon near the Taraia Peninsula,” which will be further studied.
“Amelia Earhart never gave up — she kept pushing boundaries and flying into the unknown,” Steve Schultz, Purdue’s general counsel and an expedition member, said in a statement. “That same fire fuels our search. She kept flying, and we will keep searching.”

title: Odiar Madrid
summary: Odiar Madrid Lo único a lo que aspiran quienes hablan mal de la capital, como cualquiera, por otra parte, es a no ser como los demás Odiar Madrid se ha convertido en un género literario. content:
Odiar Madrid
Lo único a lo que aspiran quienes hablan mal de la capital, como cualquiera, por otra parte, es a no ser como los demás
Odiar Madrid se ha convertido en un género literario. No uno cualquiera, sino uno de esos que aspiran a conferir prestigio y distinción a quien lo ejerce. Como el haiku o las novelas gordas. Renegar de la capital de España, despreciar su atmósfera o denunciar la hostilidad de sus gentes (así, en plural, como harían Yolanda Díaz o Julio Iglesias) ha pasado a ser una pose pretendidamente chic y cultivada. Odiar Madrid es salirse de la masa ejerciendo de masa, es reivindicarse viajero contra los turistas o defender la civilización frente a la barbarie. Odiar Madrid es elegir lubina cuando crees que todos piden chuletón.
Odiar Madrid requiere además cierta condescendencia histórica. Quien desprecia la capital reniega de la ciudad de ahora, añorando una urbe que nunca existió. Hablar mal del Madrid presente exige recordar aquella otra ciudad de cuando entonces. Pero abominar de Madrid es, sobre todo, declararles la guerra a las matemáticas, porque los datos muestran que cuanta más gente dice odiar Madrid, más personas quieren vivir en ella.
Lo único a lo que aspiran quienes hablan mal de la capital, como cualquiera, por otra parte, es a no ser como los demás. Etiam si omnes, ego non. Sin embargo, repudiar Madrid es algo tan obvio y manido como criticar El Padrino III o el Premio Planeta. Es una apuesta sin riesgo ni originalidad. Una coqueta impostura con la que ya hay quien cree que se sitúa, como en cualquier gesto menor, en el lado correcto de la historia.
Odiar Madrid se ha convertido en un reflejo, en una frase hecha, en una fórmula de cortesía con la que uno abre conversación en una cena. Es, además, una oferta de complicidad y una contraseña. Un signo de corte. Si te ofrecen repudiar tu ciudad, no puedes no aceptar. Sería como despreciar un brindis o no corresponder al saludo de un vecino. Si escuchas a alguien despotricar de Madrid, toca decir que sí: que está inhabitable, que no se puede respirar, que las calles están sucias y que hay fascistas, anarcocapitalistas y millonarios extractivistas por todas las esquinas.
Lo peor es que todo eso es cierto. Madrid es un agujero negro donde convergen casi todos los adjetivos y sus contrarios: es cara y cateta, sucia y artificial, provinciana y cosmopolita; Madrid es rancia y moderna, insomne y perezosa, desastrosa y presumida. Y ahora que todos los cursis suspiran por Lisboa y se han lanzado a criticarla, dan ganas de decirlo en todas las reuniones, aunque sea mentira: Madrid es la mejor ciudad del mundo.

title: Las izquierdas buscan impedir la reforma de la Constitución
summary: Las izquierdas buscan impedir la reforma de la Constitución Vox persigue los tres quintos para activar el cambio de la Ley Fundamental El anuncio del PSOE, Frente Amplio y otras fuerzas de izquierda territorial, diez minutos antes de la medianoche de este viernes, sobre su candidatura única al Senad...
content:
Las izquierdas buscan impedir la reforma de la Constitución
Vox persigue los tres quintos para activar el cambio de la Ley Fundamental
El anuncio del PSOE, Frente Amplio y otras fuerzas de izquierda territorial, diez minutos antes de la medianoche de este viernes, sobre su candidatura única al Senado actúa todavía como bálsamo para los sectores de izquierda frustrados por el fracaso de la coalición con Podemos. Una operación de más de seis meses concluyó con un acuerdo para ir en listas conjuntas en la cámara Alta en 43 provincias, al límite del cierre legal de la comunicación de las coaliciones; quedan fuera Cataluña y Canarias, salvo la circunscripción de La Gomera. El temor los ha unido.
La expectativa muy realista de que el PP y Vox pudieran lograr hacerse con tres quintos de la representación en la Cámara Alta convenció a los partidos, finalmente convergentes, de la imperiosa necesidad de no dispersar el voto. El trabajo de movilización y concienciación partió de intelectuales, académicos y personas progresistas sin cargos o representación orgánica en partidos. Su mensaje ha calado, muy poco a poco, hasta que el adelanto electoral les condujo a convertir las conversaciones en negociaciones.
Se trata de impedir que el PP y Vox activen el artículo 167 de la Constitución para su modificación. Ese ha sido el motor de la unidad. No se han movido sobre hipótesis teóricas, toda vez que el partido de la ultraderecha española proclama su aspiración a modificar la ley de leyes en numerosos títulos y artículos.
La Constitución no es la Biblia y puede modificarse, “pero no en ninguno de los aspectos que pretende Vox”, apuntan interlocutores que estuvieron detrás de este objetivo desde el primer momento. La recentralización de las competencias de las comunidades autónomas es una de las propuestas de la ultraderecha para dotar a la Administración central de capacidades que ahora no tiene en virtud del Título VIII de la Carta Magna. El PP no aboga por despojar de competencias a las comunidades autónomas, solo hay que pensar qué dirían al respecto presidentes como el andaluz, Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla; o la balear Marga Prohens, por poner ejemplos de comunidades con identidades muy marcadas.
Educación, Sanidad, Seguridad y Justicia son materias citadas por Vox como susceptibles de ser asumidas por el Estado. No se trata del PP, reconocen interlocutores de los partidos implicados, sino de la fuerza que pueda tener Vox y las condiciones que sea capaz de imponer a Alberto Núñez Feijóo si quiere ser investido presidente del Gobierno.
Las encuestas animan a todos los actores. A las derechas en su objetivo de romper su propia marca en el Senado; y a las izquierdas a agruparse en la papeleta Senado de Progreso para evitar que eso ocurra.
Con 210 escaños en el Congreso puede iniciarse el procedimiento de reforma; los tres quintos de la cámara para la reforma ordinaria que figura en el artículo 167 de la Constitución, que exige esas mayorías en las dos cámaras.
Tribunal Constitucional
Durante los últimos meses era evidente que el PP no tenía el menor interés en negociar con el PSOE la renovación de los cuatro miembros del Tribunal Constitucional cuyo mandato expiró el pasado mes de diciembre.
No se trataba de un bloqueo más en las imposibles negociaciones entre el PP y el PSOE, como ocurrió durante cinco años con el nombramiento de los miembros del Consejo General del Poder Judicial. En el ala izquierda de las cámaras no se tardó en caer en la cuenta de que en este caso era algo más. Según los usos y costumbres parlamentarios en el reparto de cargos, corresponde la elección de los cuatro magistrados al PP y el PSOE con la propuesta de dos cada uno, lo que debería haber ocurrido hace meses. El partido de Feijóo nunca ha desmentido la razón última de bloquear la negociación que le atribuyen los socialistas. El PP dejaba pasar el tiempo hasta que se celebraran elecciones generales, ante la previsión de que su mayoría absoluta actual en el Senado creciera hasta tener los tres quintos de la representación. Ese crecimiento les permitía poder nombrar a los cuatro magistrados del Tribunal Constitucional, o sea, aprovechar su mayoría para quedarse con todo el pastel. De esa manera, la actual mayoría progresista del Constitucional, al meter cuatro y no dos miembros conservadores, cambiaba la orientación del tribunal.
No es una razón menor la que el PP ha tenido para negarse a renovar las vacantes del alto tribunal, entre ellas la del propio presidente, Cándido Conde–Pumpido. Desde el Tribunal Constitucional se insta repetidamente al Senado para que proceda al nombramiento de los sustitutos de aquellos magistrados cuyo plazo terminó. La propia mayoría de la Mesa del Senado se ha encargado de no promover los cambios pendientes.
Esta razón también importa a los promotores de una papeleta única para el PSOE, Frente Amplio y partidos territoriales. Aspiran a que la actual mayoría progresista del Tribunal Constitucional se mantenga, pero el incentivo mayor ha sido el de tratar de evitar una mayoría de tres quintos que permita a las derechas iniciar reformas en la Constitución.
Podemos no ha estado en esta negociación, que ha concluido con la inscripción de la coalición Senado de Progreso. El sigilo de la operación no ha permitido reaccionar a Vox y al PP para hacer su propia coalición antes de que culminara el plazo de inscripciones el pasado viernes. El recurso anunciado por el partido de Abascal es su probable retirada de algunas provincias para no dividir el voto de las derechas.

title: "No hay lugar para la violencia": vehículos quemados, edificios dañados y 2.400 detenidos tras las multitudinarias protestas en Francia

content:
"No hay lugar para la violencia": vehículos quemados, edificios dañados y 2.400 detenidos tras las multitudinarias protestas en Francia
  - Autor, Redacción
  - Título del autor, BBC News Mundo
- Fecha de publicación
- Tiempo de lectura: 10 min
Francia amaneció este domingo con escenas de destrucción generalizada luego de un "día de furia" en todo el país, en el que hubo enfrentamientos entre la policía y manifestantes que protestaban por el deterioro de la educación, los altos precios y el retroceso del Estado de bienestar.
En las calles de París se veían negocios destrozados, autos quemados, bicicletas carbonizadas y montañas de vidrio y residuos.
La policía arrestó a unas 2.400 personas el sábado, mientras más de 550.000 manifestantes salían a las calles para participar en manifestaciones que fueron mayormente pacíficas.
Ante los incidentes, el presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, aseguró que "no hay lugar para la violencia" en su país.
El gobierno culpó a la "extrema izquierda" de incitar las protestas de este sábado, de cara a las elecciones presidenciales de abril, mientras que el líder del principal partido izquierdista lo acusó de "jugar con fuego" al "provocar el caos" en las calles.
El Ministerio del Interior dijo que unos 1.000 policías resultaron heridos en los disturbios.
El jefe de la cartera del Interior, Laurent Nuñez, afirmó que se registraron saqueos o intentos de saqueo en varias ciudades, entre ellas París, Ruan, Nantes, Toulouse y Marsella.
La principal manifestación tuvo lugar en la capital francesa.
Pero en la ciudad de Limoges, 400 kilómetros al sur, los bomberos debieron acudir a contener un incendio que estaba devorando el edificio del ayuntamiento, una construcción del siglo XIX.
La prefectura local informó que dos tercios de la fachada habían desaparecido y que el edificio estaba "en gran medida perdido".
El ministro del Interior declaró a periodistas que se había producido una intrusión y un incendio provocado en el interior del edificio.
Un joven "perdió una mano" por causa de un pequeño artefacto explosivo en Saint-Étienne, según informó en redes sociales Régis Juanico, alcalde de esta ciudad del sureste del país, quien añadió: "Una tragedia así nunca debería haber ocurrido".
Una amplia variedad de grupos se sumaron en todo el país después de las protestas estudiantiles registradas durante varias semanas.
Las manifestaciones comenzaron el mes pasado en escuelas de los barrios periféricos pobres del norte de París, donde la indignación por las ausencias de los profesores y el mal estado de las instalaciones se transformó rápidamente en un movimiento a escala nacional contra la desigualdad, la escasa inversión pública y el deterioro del nivel educativo.
Entre los manifestantes estaban los "chalecos amarillos" —conocidos por protestar contra la subida de los precios del combustible—, así como sindicatos y jóvenes.
Durante los disturbios se registraron daños en una comisaría de Marsella, donde las imágenes también mostraban llamas y personas enmascaradas en las calles.
El prefecto de Bocas del Ródano, departamento donde se encuentra Marsella, afirmó que 107 agentes de policía resultaron heridos —tres de ellos "muy gravemente"— tras los "saqueos y la violencia" en la ciudad.
En Lyon, en el este de Francia, los manifestantes incendiaron la oficina de turismo, informaron la agencia de noticias AFP y medios locales.
Las imágenes mostraron a los manifestantes frente al edificio en llamas, con fuego tanto en el interior como en el exterior. También destrozaron varias ventanas.
La policía local dijo que "individuos hostiles" estuvieron impidiendo que los bomberos pudieran sofocar el incendio con seguridad, mientras que los agentes de policía trabajaban para "dispersar a los grupos violentos".
"Muchos de los edificios que nos rodean han sido destrozados, y hemos visto a algunos manifestantes saqueando y lanzando botellas de vidrio, lo que agrava aún más el caos", reportó el sábado la periodista de la BBC Adina Campbell desde París.
"Serán procesados y castigados"
En una publicación en redes sociales, Macron escribió que aquellos "que han destrozado y atacado" prefecturas y comercios y "saqueado" ayuntamientos serán "procesados y castigados".
"Todos nos mantendremos unidos frente a los sembradores del caos, que solo buscan derribar nuestras instituciones e impedir que quienes expresan pacíficamente sus reivindicaciones puedan hacerlo", añadió.
Por su parte, el ministro de Interior afirmó durante una alocución por televisión que la policía contribuyó a que las manifestaciones pacíficas pudieran celebrarse, al contener a los manifestantes violentos.
Nuñez criticó a las figuras de la "extrema izquierda" que "instaron abiertamente a la revuelta" y afirmó que tendrán que asumir la responsabilidad del caos que se vivió el sábado en las calles de Francia.
El primer ministro francés aseguró que el país no se dejará "intimidar".
"A aquellos que claramente pretenden utilizar esta violencia como un 'calentamiento' previo a las elecciones presidenciales, les digo sin rodeos: no nos dejaremos intimidar. Nadie impondrá su agenda política mediante la violencia", expresó.
Lecornu le reprochó a la izquierda por "dar excusas" a los manifestantes violentos, elogió a los agentes de policía por haber hecho frente a una "violencia extrema" y añadió que merecen el apoyo de la ciudadanía.
Del otro lado, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, líder del principal partido de izquierda La France Insoumise (LFI —La Francia Insumisa—) acusó al primer ministro francés de azuzar el conflicto.
"Ha jugado con fuego. Confiando en que todo se pudra, lo único que ha conseguido es unir a toda la juventud y a los sindicatos de trabajadores. Además, sus órdenes de represión salvaje (...) han desencadenado una movilización sin precedentes en el país", escribió Mélenchon en redes sociales.

title: No agenda, no rush, no leaving San Francisco: Benchmark’s partners on investing in a frenzied market
summary: The players sometimes change. I sat down with four of Benchmark’s partners three years ago, and three of those individuals are no longer with the firm. The capital commitments have changed, too. This summer, Benchmark announced $2 billion across two funds, marking only the second time in its 31-year...
content:
The players sometimes change. I sat down with four of Benchmark’s partners three years ago, and three of those individuals are no longer with the firm. The capital commitments have changed, too. This summer, Benchmark announced $2 billion across two funds, marking only the second time in its 31-year history that it has veered from raising a far smaller vehicle.
But at this week’s TechCrunch Disrupt, the venture firm’s five partners convincingly portrayed a close-knit team that’s not about to put the pedal to the metal, even as many of their rivals do exactly that. The world may be speeding up, but they’re investing at the pace Benchmark always has: just two or three new bets per year per partner. The world is drowning in information, yet their Monday partner meetings still have no agenda. And while economic indicators point to trouble ahead, they don’t seem too bothered, seeing many of the warning signs as products of X-fueled hysteria.
Here’s what Benchmark’s full partnership — gathered publicly for the first time on our stage — had to say at the show. Some of the comments below have been edited for length and clarity; you can watch the full interview at the end of the article.
Benchmark has evolved in some ways, including a bigger core fund and a new growth fund. How do you think about adapting without losing what makes you Benchmark?
Peter Fenton: The craft that hasn’t changed is the core fund: working closely with founders at the beginning. It’s usually a 10- to 15-year commitment, [working] shoulder to shoulder, and that doesn’t scale. There’s also been inflation. We held the core fund at $500 million for 20 years, and it has just inflated to be consistent with the existing economy, which we hadn’t done and that was probably a tactical error on our part.
[As for the growth fund] it’s an expansion of our mandate. In some ways, we get permission from the ecosystem to do more than just the core early-stage business. [Not having this previously] was a fork in our eye. A number of opportunities that came to Benchmark would have returned somewhere between 10 and 1,000x to Benchmark, and we were constricted by our early-stage focus.
Are you thinking to make a handful of bets with that $1.25 billion growth fund?
PF: We all have different answers, which is the beauty of a partnership. I’d love for us to have, as that great J.P. Morgan paper puts it, the agony and ecstasy of a concentrated portfolio. If the fund is successful, one or two investments will generate 90% of the returns. So I think it’s four to six, maybe seven to eight.
Ev, you joined Benchmark late last year. You’ve worked at Founders Fund, Bond, and Kleiner Perkins. How does Benchmark differ?
Ev Randle: Every firm is ultimately a collection of the people within the firm and how they work together. Some are very hierarchical, with a 50- or 60-person investment team and investment processes that are federated into product groups. And then you have small partnerships. Very early in my career, I was drawn to small partnerships because they allow a higher level of throughput and fidelity in your conversations, where you don’t feel like you’re making decisions through some Byzantine corporate structure. You’re going out on the field together, like a sports team.
And then the other piece is: You have to find your people. You have to find people who you not only like but admire. With Benchmark, with the current crop of GPs, it was obvious that everyone liked each other and got along, but it went deeper than that. It’s a group that admires each other and learns from each other. That mix of attributes is very rare, and when I saw it, I immediately wanted to join, and I think Jack felt the same way also as a newcomer.
Jack, you joined in February, but it was just a year ago that you raised a second, $275 million fund for your own firm in what you told the Wall Street Journal took one week. You also have a hugely popular podcast. Why join Benchmark?
Jack Altman: It’s funny. I did the podcast with these guys at the start of this year, and during that podcast, obviously we talked about the commitment to being a small fund, but more than that, what I heard was that they want to be the first people who founders call, they want to be concentrated, and they just care. So much in this industry gets tied up in money and status, and what I felt from the Benchmark team then, and 10 times more as I’ve gotten to know them so well, is it’s a group that really cares about founders and helping companies. And I did enjoy being an individual investor … but in a market this crazy, I don’t know how I’d feel, figuring it out on my own. Having a group of people who are so smart and focused and driven to learn it with and from has been awesome.
I’m told you meet on Mondays with no agenda.
Chetan Puttagunta: Jack tried to make an agenda. [Laughs.]
JA: I’ve got an agenda for next Monday.
Eric Vishria: It’s weirdly arbitrary, honestly. It’s an ongoing conversation. In a time of rapid change, you’re trying to figure out what’s becoming possible that wasn’t possible six months ago, and who’s bending light. We talk about what companies we’re meeting, what piqued our interest and why, what we’re seeing in board meetings. You can try to systematize it, but one of the beauties of five people is you don’t have to. It’s a decades-long conversation that only works if you’re small and actually enjoy spending time together. After this session, we’re having dinner with one of the very few entrepreneurs who has built a multi-hundred-billion-dollar company, someone we’re not invested in, just to stretch our thinking.
CP: Part of not having an agenda is you need space to be reactive. If a founder needs help landing an executive or a strategic partnership, the five of us can be at their disposal.
You’re an equal partnership. Can one person put the kibosh on a deal?
CP: Nobody knows. We don’t have rules around it.

title: Cindy Crawford habla por primera vez tras la muerte de su hijo Presley: "Estoy más que destrozada"
summary: Cindy Crawford habla por primera vez tras la muerte de su hijo Presley: "Estoy más que destrozada" - Autor, Lisa Lambert - Título del autor, BBC News - Fecha de publicación - Tiempo de lectura: 3 min La supermodelo Cindy Crawford habló este domingo por primera vez tras la muerte de su hijo Presley G...
content:
Cindy Crawford habla por primera vez tras la muerte de su hijo Presley: "Estoy más que destrozada"
  - Autor, Lisa Lambert
  - Título del autor, BBC News
- Fecha de publicación
- Tiempo de lectura: 3 min
La supermodelo Cindy Crawford habló este domingo por primera vez tras la muerte de su hijo Presley Gerber a los 27 años y dijo que ella y su familia están "más que destrozados".
En una publicación en su cuenta de Instagram, Crawford escribió: "Estamos más que destrozados por haber perdido a nuestro amado hijo y hermano. Nos sentimos tan bendecidos por haber tenido a Presley en nuestras vidas por 27 años".
"Es un alma dulce y hermosa que amó y es amado, ahora y siempre", continuó diciendo.
"Estamos muy orgullosos de cómo se presentó ante el mundo, con bondad y vulnerabilidad".
El texto acompaña una foto de Presley en blanco y negro con plumas de ave en forma de alas.
El joven falleció el 20 de septiembre en un centro de rehabilitación en California.
La policía informó que las autoridades están investigando su muerte como una posible sobredosis.
Gerber fue modelo, al igual que su madre y su hermana menor, Kaia, e hizo su debut en la pasarela para la firma italiana Moschino con tan solo 16 años.
"Agradecemos las numerosas muestras de cariño y apoyo de tantas personas que conocen y quieren a nuestra familia, e incluso de desconocidos que sienten nuestro dolor", publicó Crawford.
"Hasta que nos volvamos a encontrar, nuestro dulce niño. Te amaremos siempre, mamá, papá y Kaia", escribió para finalizar, con un emoji de alas de ángel.
El homenaje incluye las fechas de su nacimiento y su muerte.
El médico forense del condado de Los Ángeles cataloga el caso de Gerber como pendiente de investigación adicional.
El Departamento de Policía de Santa Mónica -ciudad perteneciente al condado de Los Ángeles- ha declarado que no hay indicios de que su muerte haya sido un crimen.
El adiós de su hermana Kaia
La hermana de Gerber, Kaia, también le dedicó una publicación este domingo que incluye un video de los dos hermanos de niños bailando juntos, una foto de ellos de pie cerca del océano y una carta de cuatro páginas dirigida a "Prez" escrita con letras azules sobre un fondo celeste.
En la carta, cuenta que de niña le daba miedo perforarse las orejas, por lo que él lo hizo primero. "Siempre tú ibas primero".
"De verdad desearía que no hubieses sido tú primero esta vez", continuó.
"Estoy aprendiendo a quererte sin poder verte. A decirte algo sin tomar el teléfono para llamarte. A ser tu hermana en un mundo en el que no puedo tenderte la mano", escribió.
En los últimos años, Gerber había hablado abiertamente sobre sus problemas de salud mental y su consumo de drogas, y con frecuencia publicaba vídeos en Instagram en lo que él llamaba "Lunes de Salud Mental".
Su padre, Rande Gerber, un conocido empresario, cofundó la marca de tequila Casamigos con George Clooney.

title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
summary: Anthropic announced on Sunday that it’s creating a “public benefit fund” that will give the company “increased flexibility and scale” to support projects for societal good. Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund — structured as a wholly owned entity within the company — with...
content:
Anthropic announced on Sunday that it’s creating a “public benefit fund” that will give the company “increased flexibility and scale” to support projects for societal good.
Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund — structured as a wholly owned entity within the company — with the option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic’s value. And it offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”
There’s also the impact that AI might have on the job market, which Anthropic has already committed $200 million to study. But, the company said, “given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”
Anthropic’s announcement comes as the AI industry faces increasingly negative public sentiment, which CEO Dario Amodei has described as “fundamentally a crisis of trust.”
If you’re wondering who will actually decide which public benefits are worth funding, Anthropic said it will share more information about structure and governance in the coming months.

title: Everyone’s watching the Elizabeth Holmes documentary ‘You Can See Everything’
summary: “You Can See Everything” is already a box office sensation, with a $15 million opening weekend (based on Sunday estimates). That’s the second biggest opening weekend ever for a documentary film. The nearly three-hour movie — first revealed last month at a secretive screening at the Telluride Film Fe...
content:
“You Can See Everything” is already a box office sensation, with a $15 million opening weekend (based on Sunday estimates). That’s the second biggest opening weekend ever for a documentary film.
The nearly three-hour movie — first revealed last month at a secretive screening at the Telluride Film Festival — is only playing in 855 theaters this weekend. (In contrast, the weekend’s No. 1 movie, “Street Fighter,” is playing in 3,575.) But it had a reported 2,000 sellout screenings, and the reviews are overwhelmingly positive: “You Can See Everything” currently has a score of 99% on both Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic.
The story of Elizabeth Holmes’ rise and fall — founding blood-testing startup Theranos, attracting support from many of Silicon Valley’s biggest names, then ultimately being sentenced to 11 years in prison for defrauding investors — has already been told in books, podcasts, TV shows, and other documentaries.
But the documentary’s filmmakers were given extensive access to Holmes and her family in the month before she went to jail, and the involvement of “The Rehearsal” creator Nathan Fielder — who co-directed the film with Lance Oppenheim — made the whole thing even more intriguing.
While I haven’t seen the movie, I can at least attest to the difficulty of finding tickets in Manhattan: I spent a good chunk of yesterday trying to find a screening for tonight, and I found exactly one with seats available that weren’t in the front row. (Yes, of course I’m going.)
TechCrunch’s Amanda Silberling already got to see it on Thursday. She wrote that the enigmatic Holmes finally seems to have met her match in Fielder, a deadpan comedian who’s arguably just as strange and mysterious as she is. Fielder’s month with Holmes is apparently just the beginning of what sounds like an increasingly surreal, metatextual odyssey.
The discussion around “You Can See Everything” may be making it harder for other tech-centric films to break through. Aaron Sorkin’s “The Social Network” follow-up “The Social Reckoning” opened to a disappointing $5.5 million last weekend and has already fallen entirely out of the top 10. And Alex Gibney’s four-hour documentary “Musk” — hampered, perhaps, by resistance from social platforms and a four-hour runtime — made only $306,702 this weekend.

title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
summary: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt A soy-derived compound protected mice from high blood pressure and memory problems linked to excessive salt consumption, offering a promising new avenue for research. - Date: - October 18, 2026 - Source: - Fujita ...
content:
Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
A soy-derived compound protected mice from high blood pressure and memory problems linked to excessive salt consumption, offering a promising new avenue for research.
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- Fujita Health University
- Summary:
- Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure. It could also harm memory and social behavior. In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet. Mice given the supplement had lower blood pressure, better memory, and improved social interactions compared with mice consuming excess salt alone.
- Share:
Consuming too much salt can affect more than blood pressure. Growing evidence suggests that excessive salt intake may also interfere with memory, thinking, and emotional well-being. High salt (HS) consumption is already a major public health concern because of its connection to hypertension, but its potential effects on the brain make finding ways to reduce the damage even more important.
Researchers in Japan have identified a promising possibility in LPC70, a compound derived from soy. Previous research found that this ingredient could reduce high blood pressure and cognitive problems associated with a high-salt diet (HSD) in mice. The latest study takes a closer look at how it works, revealing that the compound influences important chemical signals in the brain and kidneys.
How a Soy Compound May Counter the Effects of Excess Salt
The research centers on prostaglandins (PGs), signaling molecules made from a fatty acid called arachidonic acid (AA). These substances act much like local hormones, helping regulate essential functions throughout the body.
In the cardiovascular system, prostaglandins help control blood pressure by balancing the widening and narrowing of blood vessels. Their effects in the brain are more complicated. Depending on which receptors they activate, they can trigger signals that either protect nerve cells or contribute to harmful processes, potentially affecting memory, thinking, and emotional responses.
LPC70 is a form of soy lysolecithin in which lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) accounts for more than 70% of the phospholipids. Although earlier experiments showed that LPC70 could ease salt-related hypertension and cognitive difficulties, scientists had not fully understood the mechanisms responsible, particularly its influence on prostaglandin signaling.
To investigate, a research team led by Professor Akihiro Mouri and Dr. Hisayoshi Kubota, working with Dr. Kazuhiro Kagotani, examined how LPC70 affected these signaling pathways in mice consuming a high-salt diet.
Dr. Kubota, the study's first author, played a central role in the experiments. He assessed blood pressure, monitored behavioral changes, and analyzed molecular activity associated with prostaglandins. His work helped clarify how LPC70 produces different effects in the organs involved in salt-related cardiovascular and cognitive problems.
Prof. Mouri and Dr. Kubota are affiliated with the Department of Regulatory Science for Evaluation and Development of Pharmaceuticals & Devices at Fujita Health University Graduate School of Medical Science, as well as the International Center for Brain Science (ICBS) at Fujita Health University in Japan. Dr. Kagotani is affiliated with Tsuji Oil Mills Co., Ltd, in Japan and the Tsuji Health and Beauty Science Laboratory at Mie University, Japan.
The findings were released online on May 14, 2026, and published in Volume 197 of Neurochemistry International on July 1, 2026.
"We wanted to understand the role of LPC70 in coordinating changes in PG signaling across organ systems," mentioned Prof. Mouri. "Our study originated from a collaborative research project with Tsuji Oil Mills Co., Ltd, a company that develops naturally derived food ingredients," he added.
Soy Compound Improves Blood Pressure and Memory in Mice
As expected, mice that consumed a high-salt diet developed elevated blood pressure. However, the consequences extended beyond their cardiovascular health.
The animals also became less socially interactive and had difficulty recognizing objects they had encountered before, indicating problems with memory. Interestingly, their general movement and anxiety-like behavior showed no substantial changes. This pattern suggests that excessive salt selectively disrupted more complex cognitive and social functions rather than causing widespread behavioral impairment.
When researchers supplemented the animals' diets with LPC70, several of these effects were reduced. Blood pressure improved, and the mice performed better on tests of social interaction and object recognition memory.
These improvements prompted the researchers to examine what was happening inside the animals' kidneys and brains.
Different Protective Effects in the Kidneys and Brain
In the kidneys, a high-salt diet increased the expression of two components involved in prostaglandin signaling: cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and the PGE2 receptor EP3. Both may contribute to the development of high blood pressure associated with excessive salt consumption.
LPC70 reduced these salt-related increases, suggesting that the compound helps correct changes in kidney signaling that can interfere with normal blood pressure regulation.
The researchers found a different response in the prefrontal cortex, a brain region essential for thinking, memory, and social behavior.
Excess salt reduced the expression of the PGD2 receptor DP1, which plays a role in protective and anti-inflammatory signaling in the brain. LPC70 restored expression of this receptor without changing DP2, another receptor associated with potentially harmful effects on nerve cells.

title: El papa León XIV hace su primera aparición pública tras ser operado por un cáncer de pulmón y "no hay motivos clínicos" que impidan su viaje a Sudamérica
summary: El papa León XIV hace su primera aparición pública tras ser operado por un cáncer de pulmón y "no hay motivos clínicos" que impidan su viaje a Sudamérica - Autor, Redacción - Título del autor, BBC News Mundo - Fecha de publicación - Tiempo de lectura: 3 min Vestido de blanco y con una sonrisa, el pa...
content:
El papa León XIV hace su primera aparición pública tras ser operado por un cáncer de pulmón y "no hay motivos clínicos" que impidan su viaje a Sudamérica
  - Autor, Redacción
  - Título del autor, BBC News Mundo
- Fecha de publicación
- Tiempo de lectura: 3 min
Vestido de blanco y con una sonrisa, el papa León XIV se asomó por la ventana de su estudio, en el Vaticano, para pronunciar el Ángelus y agradecer las oraciones de los feligreses por su salud.
Este domingo, desde el Palacio Apostólico, el pontífice hizo su primera aparición pública después de que fuese operado.
El Papa fue diagnosticado con cáncer de pulmón tras someterse, el martes, a una cirugía torácica para extirparle un nódulo que le había sido detectado unos días antes, informó el Vaticano.
En la operación, que duró 90 minutos y que se realizó en el Policlínico Gemelli, de Roma, se le extirpó el lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho.
El sábado, los médicos le dieron de alta tras realizar análisis de sangre, radiografías de tórax y otras evaluaciones clínicas.
En horas de la tarde, el pontífice salió del hospital caminando, sonriente y saludando a quienes se habían concentrado afuera del hospital.
El domingo, con voz firme, León XIV se dirigió a los miles de feligreses que estaban reunidos en la Plaza de San Pedro, así como a los que siguieron la transmisión desde diferentes países, y les agradeció por sus oraciones.
"Habiendo superado esta fase delicada... Ahora reanudaré gradualmente mis actividades, siempre con la ayuda de Dios y sus oraciones", indicó.
En el Ángelus, el Papa recordó el Evangelio de Mateo que presenta una de las enseñanzas más famosas de Jesús: "Dadle al César lo que es del César y a Dios lo que es de Dios".
"Un paciente ideal"
El sábado, Vatican News publicó una entrevista con el cirujano Stefano Margaritora, quien operó a León XIV.
El médico indicó que, en términos generales, el estado de salud del Papa es "bueno".
"La reexpansión del pulmón después de la intervención está siguiendo los plazos previstos habitualmente".
Para que se dé una recuperación completa, se necesitarán unos diez días, señaló y describió al pontífice como "un paciente ideal".
Consultado sobre el viaje que León XIV tiene previsto hacer en América Latina, entre el 6 y el 17 de noviembre, Margaritora se mostró optimista.
"Después de este tipo de intervención considero que se necesitan un par de semanas para lograr una recuperación física verdaderamente completa. Por tanto, dado que ya ha transcurrido casi una semana, en definitiva, creo que el Papa podrá estar plenamente recuperado dentro de unos diez días más", dijo.
"En cuanto a un viaje largo, con desplazamientos en avión, que tendrá lugar dentro de aproximadamente tres semanas, diría que no hay motivos clínicos por los que no se pueda realizar".
Muchos de los miles de fieles que estaban en la Plaza de San Pedro se mostraron felices de ver al Papa. Varios gritaron y lo aplaudieron.
Una monja católica se arrodilló y lloró, cuenta la agencia de noticias Reuters.
Muy cerca de ella, un grupo de otras monjas alzó un cartel que decía: "Mis mejores deseos, Santo Padre. Te queremos y estamos rezando por ti".

title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
summary: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood A new study hints that eating blueberries daily could help improve mood in older adults, potentially through surprising effects on the gut microbiome. - Date: - October 18, 2026 - Source: - Hebrew SeniorLife Hinda and Arthur Marc...
content:
Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
A new study hints that eating blueberries daily could help improve mood in older adults, potentially through surprising effects on the gut microbiome.
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- Hebrew SeniorLife Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research
- Summary:
- Eating blueberries every day could have surprising effects on mood, according to a small study that found greater reductions in depressive symptoms among older adults who consumed the fruit for three months. Researchers also detected changes in gut microbial enzymes, suggesting a possible gut-brain connection, although the mood benefits were not statistically significant compared with a placebo.
- Share:
A small pilot study suggests that eating blueberries every day may influence gut bacteria and potentially affect mood in older adults. Participants who consumed blueberries regularly experienced a greater and more consistent reduction in depressive symptoms, along with subtle changes in genes associated with gut microbial enzymes.
However, the improvements in depressive symptoms were not statistically significant when compared with the placebo group. Although the findings do not establish that blueberries can relieve depression, they offer preliminary clues about a possible connection between blueberry consumption, the gut microbiome, and mental health.
"Fiber and anthocyanins in blueberries have potential to modify the gut microbiome and metabolites that are relevant to depression in older adults," said lead author Courtney L. Millar, PhD, assistant scientist II at Hebrew SeniorLife's Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research and assistant professor of medicine at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School. "Our objective was to preliminarily determine the effect of blueberry consumption on the gut microbiome, metabolites, and depressive symptoms."
Testing the Effects of Daily Blueberry Consumption
To investigate the potential connection, researchers recruited adults aged 65 and older who were physically inactive and experiencing mild depressive symptoms. The pilot study used a randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm, placebo-controlled design to evaluate whether consuming blueberries could influence gut microbes and mood.
Over three months, participants consumed either 48 grams of blueberry powder each day (approximately two cups of fresh berries) or a matching placebo powder.
Researchers examined the participants' gut microbiomes using metagenomic sequencing, which allowed them to measure the abundance of different microbial species and genes. They also used liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry to analyze gut-derived fecal short-chain fatty acids, compounds produced through microbial activity. Depressive symptoms were assessed using validated questionnaires administered before and after the three-month intervention.
Blueberries Linked to Subtle Changes in Gut Microbial Activity
A total of 18 participants completed the study. Most were women, and the group was predominantly white (placebo group, n = 8; mean age: 75 ± 6; blueberry group, n = 10; mean age: 71 ± 4).
Despite the encouraging pattern in depressive symptoms among participants consuming blueberries, the researchers found no statistically significant difference in mood improvements between the blueberry and placebo groups.
The gut microbiome results also revealed a mixed picture. The overall abundance of microbial species, MetaCyc metabolic pathways, and short-chain fatty acid metabolites remained unchanged.
However, researchers identified statistically significant changes within the blueberry group in the abundance of genes associated with several gut microbial enzymes. One of these was EC 3.6.3.31 Polyamine Transporting ATPase, which is involved in the production of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a neurotransmitter that plays a role in brain signaling.
These findings suggest that blueberries may influence specific aspects of gut microbial function even without producing measurable changes in the overall composition of the microbiome. Larger studies will be needed to determine whether these changes are connected to meaningful improvements in mood or depressive symptoms.
The study, "A pilot study of daily blueberry intake modulates the gut microbiota enzyme commissions in older, sedentary adults with mild depressive symptoms," was published in the Journal of Nutrition, Health and Aging.
Other contributors included Mohit P. Chopra, MD, of the Deanna and Sidney Wolk Center for Memory Health at Hebrew SeniorLife and the Department of Psychiatry at UMass Chan Medical School; Xochitl Morgan, PhD, and Emily A. Green, PhD, of the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health; Alex Wolfe of the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research at Hebrew SeniorLife; Kerry A. Pierce of the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; and Lidan Gao, PhD, and Christopher N. Blesso, PhD, of the Department of Nutritional Sciences at the University of Connecticut.
Additional contributors were Alyssa B. Dufour, PhD, of the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research at Hebrew SeniorLife and the Department of Medicine at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School; Douglas P. Kiel, MD, MPH, of the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research at Hebrew SeniorLife, Harvard Medical School, and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; and Lewis A. Lipsitz, MD, of the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research at Hebrew SeniorLife and professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School.

title: Scientists link a strange sugar in red meat to a 63% higher diabetes risk
summary: Scientists link a strange sugar in red meat to a 63% higher diabetes risk - Date: - October 18, 2026 - Source: - European Association for the Study of Diabetes - Summary: - A study of nearly 90,000 adults found that people consuming the most of a little-known sugar found in red meat had a 63% higher...
content:
Scientists link a strange sugar in red meat to a 63% higher diabetes risk
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- European Association for the Study of Diabetes
- Summary:
- A study of nearly 90,000 adults found that people consuming the most of a little-known sugar found in red meat had a 63% higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Scientists suspect the sugar may trigger chronic inflammation, potentially revealing a hidden connection between red meat and diabetes that goes beyond weight gain.
- Share:
A sugar naturally present in red meat may help explain why eating these foods has been associated with a higher risk of type 2 diabetes. Preliminary findings from a large observational study suggest that people who consume the most of this sugar face a substantially greater risk of developing the disease, potentially because of its effects on the immune system and chronic inflammation.
The sugar, known as N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc), is particularly common in beef and lamb. Researchers found that participants with the highest intake of meat-derived Neu5Gc had a 63% higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes (T2D) compared with those who consumed the least.
The association remained statistically significant after researchers accounted for several established diabetes risk factors, including physical activity, overall diet, smoking, and existing health conditions. It became weaker after body mass index (BMI) was also considered, but remained significant.
The findings were presented at the Annual Meeting of The European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) in Milan, Italy.
“Our findings support chronic inflammation as a specific mechanism linking red meat consumption with T2D, partly beyond the amount of red meat a person eats and partly independent of body fat,” said lead author Dr. Leopold Fezeu from the Université Sorbonne Paris Nord, Bobigny, France.
The researchers also observed that diabetes risk generally increased with greater consumption of meat-derived Neu5Gc, particularly among those with the highest exposure.
“Although we do not know exactly what levels of Neu5Gc trigger an immune response, our data suggest that higher intakes of meat-derived Neu5Gc are associated with a progressively higher risk of T2D.”
Why a Sugar in Red Meat May Trigger Inflammation
Neu5Gc is produced naturally by most mammals, but humans lost the ability to make it following an ancient mutation in the CMAH gene. Despite this evolutionary change, the sugar can still enter the human body through food.
It occurs in red meat (particularly beef and lamb), with smaller amounts also found in dairy products.
After Neu5Gc is consumed, the body absorbs it and can incorporate it into human tissues. Because humans do not naturally produce the molecule, the immune system may recognize it as foreign. Scientists classify it as a xeno-autoantigen, a foreign substance that becomes incorporated into the body's own tissues and can provoke an immune reaction.
In response, the immune system produces antibodies against Neu5Gc. The resulting prolonged immune activity, called xenosialitis (xenosialitis), has previously been associated with cardiovascular disease and cancer.
Researchers suspect that this persistent inflammatory response could also contribute to type 2 diabetes. However, before this investigation, no large prospective study had examined whether dietary Neu5Gc might promote diabetes through chronic inflammation.
Nearly 90,000 Adults Studied Over Several Years
To investigate the possible connection, the scientists analyzed dietary and health information from 89,953 adults participating in NutriNet-Santé, a large French observational study that follows people over time to examine how nutrition and lifestyle influence health.
Participants were 42 years old on average, and 79% were women. None had type 2 diabetes or cancer when they entered the study.
Each person completed three 24-hour dietary records. The research team then used a validated food database to calculate how much Neu5Gc participants were likely consuming based on the measured amounts of the sugar in different foods.
The analysis included a broad range of red meats, such as beef, lamb, pork, rabbit, goat, and game. Processed meats (such as bacon, sausages and cured meats) were evaluated as a separate category, while dairy products were analyzed independently.
Using the dietary information, the researchers estimated total Neu5Gc intake from all reported foods. They then ranked participants separately by sex according to their intake of meat-derived Neu5Gc and divided them into five equally sized groups (quintiles).
Diabetes risk was compared across these groups, using those with the lowest intake as the reference.
During a median follow-up period of 7.2 years, researchers recorded 966 new cases of type 2 diabetes.
Higher Red Meat Sugar Intake Linked to 63% Greater Diabetes Risk
The results showed a significant relationship between meat-derived Neu5Gc consumption and the likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes. The association became particularly pronounced among participants with the highest estimated intake.
Compared with the lowest intake group, individuals in the highest group had a 63% greater risk of developing the disease. Those in the second-highest group had a 41% greater risk (men and women combined).
These estimates accounted for potentially influential factors, including age, sex, exercise habits, overall dietary quality, smoking, and existing medical conditions.
The researchers also examined how much meat participants typically consumed.
Among men in the highest Neu5Gc intake group, median red meat consumption was 97 grams daily (136 g including processed meat). For women, the corresponding amount was 73 grams (96 g).
By comparison, men in the lowest intake group consumed a median of just 5 grams of red meat per day (21 g), while women consumed 0 grams (9 g).

title: Scientists discover a surprising twist in Japan's 7,300-year-old volcanic apocalypse
summary: Scientists discover a surprising twist in Japan's 7,300-year-old volcanic apocalypse - Date: - October 18, 2026 - Source: - Lund University - Summary: - A catastrophic volcanic eruption 7,300 years ago devastated Japan, but new research reveals that its impact on prehistoric populations was far more...
content:
Scientists discover a surprising twist in Japan's 7,300-year-old volcanic apocalypse
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- Lund University
- Summary:
- A catastrophic volcanic eruption 7,300 years ago devastated Japan, but new research reveals that its impact on prehistoric populations was far more complex than previously believed. While some communities disappeared or declined, others unexpectedly flourished as survivors migrated, adapted, and found new ways to thrive.
- Share:
A massive volcanic eruption that struck Japan about 7,300 years ago had a devastating impact on prehistoric communities, but its aftermath was far more complicated than scientists once believed. While some populations declined or disappeared from affected areas, others continued to grow despite the destruction.
An international research team led by Lund University investigated how the Kikai-Akahoya eruption changed population patterns across Japan. Their findings challenge the idea that the disaster either completely wiped out nearby communities or left them largely unaffected. Instead, the researchers uncovered a surprising mix of population decline, migration, adaptation, and growth.
A Catastrophic Volcanic Eruption in Ancient Japan
When the Kikai-Akahoya volcano erupted beneath the sea approximately 7,300 years ago, Japan was home to Jomon communities that depended on hunting and gathering for survival.
"This eruption must have been devastating, exploding out of the seabed with little warning. It battered the Japanese islands with powerful earthquakes and enormous tsunamis, and then blanketed the landscape with meters of volcanic ash," explains senior author Peter Jordan, professor in archaeology at Lund University.
For decades, archaeologists have disagreed about what happened to the people living near the eruption. One theory describes an almost complete apocalypse, with human populations abruptly disappearing from areas closest to the eruption. Another suggests that some communities managed to survive even relatively close to the disaster.
The new findings indicate that neither explanation fully captures what happened. The eruption severely damaged ecosystems, forced people from their homes, and made some regions uninhabitable. Yet evidence also points to remarkable adaptability among survivors, with certain populations actually increasing after the catastrophe.
"The disaster caused major loss of life. However, survivors migrated, forged new social relations, innovated new kinds of economy, and appear to have found creative ways to exist and later thrive in the new post-disaster conditions," says lead author Enrico Crema, professor at Cambridge University.
How the Volcanic Disaster Reshaped Japan's Population
The researchers identified striking differences in how communities across Japan responded to the eruption.
In southern Kyushu, Jomon populations had already been shrinking long before the volcano erupted. By the time the disaster occurred, relatively few people remained in the region, which was primarily visited by highly mobile groups of foragers.
Northern Kyushu followed a very different pattern. Its population had been increasing before the eruption, and that growth continued through the catastrophe and afterward, even though the surrounding ecosystems experienced extensive and lasting damage. The researchers suggest that people fleeing the most severely affected regions may have contributed to this unexpected population growth.
Evidence also indicates that survivors who had lived inland relocated toward the northern coast. Marine ecosystems in these areas recovered relatively quickly, providing valuable food resources. By developing new ways to take advantage of the sea's abundance, these communities may have supported further population growth.
Unexpected Effects Far From the Volcano
Perhaps even more surprising, the researchers identified population changes in parts of Japan much farther from the eruption.
These distant regions had experienced population growth before the catastrophe, but afterward, that growth stalled or even reversed. Such widespread demographic consequences had not previously been recognized.
Several possible explanations could account for these changes. The eruption may have caused temporary climate disruptions that affected communities across Japan. Another possibility involves severe tooth wear among deer and wild boar, two important food sources for the Jomon (possibly a consequence of the animals grazing in ash-covered landscapes). Other volcanic effects on human health and living conditions may also have contributed.
Together, these findings suggest that the consequences of a massive natural disaster can extend well beyond the areas experiencing the most immediate destruction.
According to Jordan, the results demonstrate that the effects of catastrophes are rarely straightforward. Even when faced with overwhelming destruction, human communities can respond in different ways, depending on their circumstances and the choices available to them.
"This study helps in creating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes. Even in the most impossible situations, survivors and communities have choices, however limited: they need to act and make decisions; they need to adjust, collaborate, and find new connections and social networks," he concludes.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Lund University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Enrico R. Crema, Mitsuhiro Kuwahata, Junzo Uchiyama, Ari Junno, Felix Riede, Peter D. Jordan. Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan. Science Advances, 2026; 12 (42) DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.aeh7197

title: Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief
summary: Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief - Date: - October 18, 2026 - Source: - The Mount Sinai Hospital / Mount Sinai School of Medicine - Summary: - Researchers have uncovered three brain pathways linked to lasting improvements in people receiving deep brain stim...
content:
Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief
- Date:
- October 18, 2026
- Source:
- The Mount Sinai Hospital / Mount Sinai School of Medicine
- Summary:
- Researchers have uncovered three brain pathways linked to lasting improvements in people receiving deep brain stimulation for severe, treatment-resistant depression. They also discovered that patients who failed to improve after two years shared a striking pattern: insufficient stimulation of a crucial brain connection. The findings suggest that millimeters in electrode placement could make a major difference in treatment outcomes.
- Share:
Scientists at Mount Sinai have identified three important brain connections associated with long-term improvement in patients receiving deep brain stimulation (DBS) for severe depression that has not responded to conventional treatments. The discovery could help researchers make this experimental therapy more precise and effective.
Published October 1 in the American Journal of Psychiatry, the research examined the largest group of patients assembled across multiple independent cohorts to date who had received subcallosal cingulate deep brain stimulation (SCC DBS) for treatment-resistant depression.
The researchers found that lasting improvements were consistently associated with electrical stimulation reaching three specific white matter pathways: the cingulum bundle, forceps minor, and medial uncinate fasciculus/ventral amygdalofugal pathways.
These findings strengthen the case for using detailed maps of the brain's connections to determine exactly where electrodes should be implanted, rather than choosing their positions based primarily on anatomical landmarks. Known as connectome-based targeting, this strategy has already helped shape the ongoing Abbott TRANSCEND clinical trial, a randomized, controlled study that uses individualized brain connectivity maps to guide SCC DBS treatment.
"This study underscores the importance of individualized surgical targeting for achieving optimal outcomes with deep brain stimulation for depression," said Helen Mayberg, MD, Mount Sinai Professor in Neurotherapeutics and founding Director of the Nash Family Center for Advanced Circuit Therapeutics at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. "In any randomized controlled trial of a neuromodulation treatment, precise lead placement and confirmation that the intended brain target has been engaged are essential first steps. We still have much to learn about which patients are most likely to benefit from stimulation of this particular target, but developing imaging-based signatures that can match patients to their optimal treatment remains a central goal of our research."
How Deep Brain Stimulation Targets Severe Depression
For people with treatment-resistant depression, standard therapies have failed to provide adequate relief. Researchers are investigating deep brain stimulation as a possible treatment for individuals living with severe, persistent symptoms.
The procedure involves surgically placing electrodes inside the brain to deliver controlled electrical signals to circuits involved in depression. However, positioning the electrodes correctly remains one of the greatest challenges.
Electrical stimulation does not simply affect the brain tissue closest to an implanted electrode. It can also influence larger networks through the white matter pathways that connect different brain regions. As a result, two patients with electrodes implanted in nearly identical locations may experience very different outcomes depending on which connections are actually stimulated.
Earlier research from Mount Sinai and Emory University helped establish the importance of these networks. In studies published between 2014 and 2023 in Biological Psychiatry, Molecular Psychiatry, and Nature, the teams identified white matter pathways associated with successful SCC DBS treatment and developed a method for planning electrode placement using brain connectivity maps.
The latest investigation sought to determine whether those connections were also important in patients treated at other research centers. Scientists also wanted to understand whether differences in the pathways reached by stimulation could help account for patients who did not benefit.
Three Brain Connections Linked to Lasting Improvement
To investigate, the researchers examined information from several clinical studies, including the BROADEN trial and a patient cohort at the University of Toronto, where SCC DBS was originally developed.
They used computer models of the electrical fields generated by implanted electrodes alongside maps of brain connectivity. This allowed them to estimate which pathways received stimulation and compare those patterns across different patient groups.
The results showed a consistent relationship between sustained improvement and stimulation of the cingulum bundle, forceps minor, and medial uncinate fasciculus/ventral amygdalofugal pathways.
One finding was especially notable. Across the study sites, patients who had not responded to treatment after two years showed a lack of stimulation engagement with the left cingulum bundle.
The researchers did not investigate whether moving electrodes to reach this pathway would improve those patients' symptoms. Nevertheless, the pattern offers a possible explanation for why apparently similar electrode placements can produce different results. An electrode might be positioned in the correct general region but still fail to activate all the connections associated with lasting improvement.
"This study addresses an important question in DBS: not simply which area of the brain to stimulate, but which connections within that area need to be engaged," said Brian Kopell, MD, Director of the Center for Neuromodulation at Mount Sinai. "For a network disorder such as depression, millimeters can determine whether stimulation reaches the pathways we intend to modulate. Identifying and rep

title: Perdí mi cabello por la quimioterapia y ahora las estrellas llevan las pelucas que diseño
summary: Perdí mi cabello por la quimioterapia y ahora las estrellas llevan las pelucas que diseño - Autor, Ella Kipling - Fecha de publicación - Tiempo de lectura: 4 min Cuando a Antonia Okonma Shittu le dijeron que tenía esclerosis múltiple (EM) y que tendría que usar una silla de ruedas en el plazo de un ...
content:
Perdí mi cabello por la quimioterapia y ahora las estrellas llevan las pelucas que diseño
  - Autor, Ella Kipling
- Fecha de publicación
- Tiempo de lectura: 4 min
Cuando a Antonia Okonma Shittu le dijeron que tenía esclerosis múltiple (EM) y que tendría que usar una silla de ruedas en el plazo de un año, se negó a aceptarlo.
La joven de 26 años, que combinaba trabajos como actriz con un empleo en un centro de llamadas, dijo que el diagnóstico fue un "punto de inflexión importantísimo" en su vida.
"Realmente te hace reflexionar sobre lo que quieres hacer en la vida", dijo.
Recordó lo que le gustaba hacer de niña —peinar— y decidió usar el impacto del diagnóstico para convertir su pasión en un negocio.
Antonia, que creció en una conjunto de viviendas sociales en el oeste de Londres, compró dos pelucas y empezó a ir de puerta en puerta vendiéndolas desde el maletero de su auto.
Casi dos décadas después, es dueña de una marca multimillonaria, con clientas de alto perfil como la leyenda del tenis Serena Williams, la actriz Niecey Nash y la modelo Naomi Campbell. La semana pasada ganó un premio Black British Business Award.
Antonia, que ahora tiene 44 años, sigue luchando contra sus problemas de salud, ya que también le han diagnosticado la enfermedad de Graves, una afección autoinmune, e insuficiencia cardíaca, pero espera que su experiencia dirigiendo un gran negocio de peluquería mientras acude a citas médicas pueda inspirar a otras mujeres.
"No me sentía yo misma después de perder el pelo"
Antonia afirma que detectó un hueco en el mercado cuando trabajaba en televisión y cine. Recuerda que estaba rodeada de pelucas "horribles".
"Las mujeres querían pelucas de aspecto natural y simplemente no las había. ¡Parecían cascos!", dice.
Antonia creó una página de Facebook y empezó a anunciarse en una página de anuncios clasificados. "Tenía recursos muy limitados. No contaba con ningún inversor. Vengo de orígenes muy humildes".
Según ella, su experiencia con la esclerosis múltiple ha contribuido a su éxito. Antonia perdió el cabello durante la quimioterapia tras un trasplante de médula ósea, por lo que sabe lo que es estar completamente calva.
Esto le permitió conectar más profundamente con sus clientas, explica, ya que comprende la pérdida de control que sienten algunas mujeres cuando pierden el cabello.
"No me sentía yo misma", dice, "pero poder ponerme una peluca que se parezca a mi pelo antes, o al estilo que tenía, es como si pudiera volver a sentirme yo misma".
Ver a una mujer ponerse una peluca y que "se le ilumina toda la cara" puede ser "muy, muy gratificante", dice.
"Cuando nos sentimos bien con nosotros mismos... tenemos más confianza, podemos lograr más. Sentía que estaba cambiando el mundo, una persona cada vez".
Equilibrar la salud y los negocios
Si bien el negocio de Antonia, A-List Lace Hair, ha crecido de forma imparable y ahora cuenta con salones en Londres y Nueva York, ha tenido que lidiar con las consecuencias de sus problemas de salud.
Debido a su esclerosis múltiple padece fatiga y usa silla de ruedas, pero afirma que esto no ha frenado su éxito. Simplemente ha cambiado la forma en que dirige su negocio.
"Antes pensaba que ser una buena emprendedora consistía en poder hacer todo lo que pudiera por mí misma", dice.
"Debido a mis problemas de salud, hay días en los que literalmente no siento las piernas, las siento como gelatina; hay días en los que estoy completamente agotada después de dormir, me despierto totalmente destrozada".
Esto la ha obligado a "confiar en otras personas y a fortalecerse mediante la formación de un equipo".
Como mujer de negocios, estar en silla de ruedas a veces puede hacer que Antonia se sienta "más pequeña", ya que la gente a menudo tiene que mirarla desde arriba en los eventos del sector.
"La gente suele sorprenderse cuando empiezo a hablar de mi negocio, como si pensaran: '¿Cómo has conseguido todo esto en silla de ruedas?'".
Antonia, quien tiene tres hijos pequeños, dice que ser subestimada puede ser algo bueno, y quiere hablar abiertamente sobre su salud para inspirar a otras mujeres.
Dice que antes se sentía "débil" debido a su discapacidad, pero ahora siente que ha ganado "mucha fuerza" al compartir en línea su experiencia.
Cuando se le pregunta qué le diría a otra mujer que teme que su edad, discapacidad o salud puedan interponerse en su camino hacia el éxito, responde: "La animaría a que simplemente empiece".
"Puede que no tengas control sobre tu salud, puede que no sepas qué te depara el mañana y puede que no cuentes con todos los recursos. Pero empieza con lo que sí tienes y veamos qué puede pasar después".
